full_judgment: 5. We have very often expressed out surprise looking at these sorts of orders which discloses no basis or reasoning and is therefore, to be avoided but to no result. However, in considering the facts and circumstances and when the question of identity of the land over which the boundary wall is sought to be erected to be situated in CS Plot No. 102 or in CS Plot No. 101 which CS Khatian had been prepared years ago, a local investigation by a survey knowing Advocate was a necessity. It was necessary to resolve the dispute and for that matter it was even necessary for the court itself to understand the pleadings of the parties and to decide the matter in accordance with law and not on pious wishes, surmises and conjectures. The court has a discretion in passing such an order allowing or not allowing a pleader commissioner but the discretion should be exercised judicially and not fancifully. We find that to be just and proper that the prayer for local investigation by a survey knowing Advocate be allowed and it need be ordered so by the court below and we order a local inspection by a pleader commissioner by setting aside the impugned order.
